security is the most important factor in determining trustworthiness of an electronic commerce site.

(1) security features were the most important trust index when purchasing goods and service over the Web, (2) consumers' perceptions of trustworthines of Web merchants did now parallel experts' evaluation, and (3) consumers' decision whether or not to provide private information is based on their perceptions of a marketer' trustworthiness, irrespective of whether the marketer is electronic or land and electronic.

the role of trustworthiness in electronic and land commerce, with a focus on the relative importance of four common trust indicators (third party privacy seals, privacy statements, third party security seals and security features).

the relative importance of four common trust measures and their impact on consumers' perceptions of trustworthness of a Web site and their intentions to purchase from that site.

consumers' perceptions of trustworthness are not necessarily related to the presence or absence of the trust indices studied.

the most important factor for consumers when making the decision whether to purchase from an electronic merchant is the perceived trustworthiness of the merchant, which is based on the consumers' perception of the security and privacy measures taken by the merchant.

the trust of a consumer in an electronic merchant is based upon the consumer's perception of the merchant's trustworthiness, and that the consumer's perception is influenced by the consumer's perception that the merchant's Web site is secure.
